articles.title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker responds to clip of emotional rookie: 'This isn't a fairy tale'
articles.summary: Cowboys brass emphasized how Parker would revitalize their unit's communication. In the season opener, communication challenges produced "blatant busts sever...
articles.body:
First-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker knew when he took the job that the Dallas Cowboys spotlight would be bright.

Coaching the Cowboys presents a chance to show his and his defenders' talents often on a national stage. The realities of the Cowboys spotlight also mean narratives often get magnified beyond what most NFL markets experience.

One such narrative came Wednesday night, when a social media user posted a clip from the "Sunday Night Football" broadcast of the Cowboys' 28-20 loss to the New York Giants . In it, Parker appears to talk sternly to third-round rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham .

In the clip, Barham is visibly emotional and, at one point, stands up from the bench, shaking off Parker, who appears to be trying to continue the conversation with Barham.

The video had more than 2.5 million views in less than 24 hours.

"I think he was frustrated," Parker told reporters of Barham. "It's his first NFL game, and things aren't going to be perfect. This isn't a fairy tale at all. And I think that Jaishawn cares as much as anybody in that locker room about us winning, No. 1, but, No. 2, our defensive performance.

"So he was a little frustrated with himself and frustrated with our side of the ball as we played. But I don't think anybody in our building has any doubt of what he's going to do coming real soon. So we don't have any reservations about his mentality. We welcome that passion. Have to channel it better. And that's something that young players have to go through. It's a natural progression.

"We have a lot of confidence in Jaishawn."

The Cowboys allowed 394 yards in their opening loss to the Giants, the seventh-most of any team in Week 1. No defense fared worse on third down than the Cowboys' 81.82% allowance, as New York completed 9-of-11 on third. That allowed the Giants to control the clock and keep Dallas' high-powered offense sidelined through much of the second half.

Only two teams, the Los Angeles Chargers and Tennessee Titans , held the ball for less time than the Cowboys' 23:20.

Barham recorded six tackles, including three solo tackles and one tackle for loss, in his NFL debut. He allowed a 118.7 passer rating when targeted, per Pro Football Reference's advanced metrics, and registered a 14.3% missed tackle rate while allowing a touchdown.

During training camp, Cowboys brass emphasized how Parker would revitalize their unit's communication. In the season opener, communication challenges produced "blatant busts several times on film," one NFC talent evaluator told Yahoo Sports after watching it.

Barham is far from the first Cowboys player to draw social media attention for an emotional sideline moment. Cowboys receivers CeeDee Lamb and Dez Bryant have similarly generated attention, including one emotional conversation between Lamb and quarterback Dak Prescott after a "Sunday Night Football" game against the San Francisco 49ers .

The Cowboys host the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

articles.title: Aaron Donald's Status for Rams-Giants Updated By McVay as NFL Star 'Chomping at the Bit' to Play
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said that defensive tackle Aaron Donald is "obviously chomping at the bit" to play in the team's Week 2 matchup with the New York Giants, according to ESPN's Sarah Barshop.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said that defensive tackle Aaron Donald is "obviously chomping at the bit" to play in the team's Week 2 matchup with the New York Giants, according to ESPN's Sarah Barshop .

"What we are hopeful is, is that we'll have some good work today and tomorrow and then hopefully he's feeling good enough," McVay explained, per Barshop. "And if he says he's ready to go, then we'll be excited to see him [on MNF]."

Donald came out of retirement to join the Rams ahead of the 2026 season, but didn't travel with them to Australia for a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year is still ramping up as he prepares to make his first appearance in an NFL game since his 2023 campaign.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport previously reported that the "hope" is Donald will be available to suit up against the Giants.

The 35-year-old was a full participant in Los Angeles' practice on Thursday, per Stu Jackson of the team's official website.

Even though the Rams boasted an imposing front seven prior to Donald's arrival, they're suddenly in need of more help along their defensive line.

Los Angeles failed to sack 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy in its lopsided Week 1 defeat. San Francisco also amassed 174 rush yards as a team, averaging 5.8 yards per carry.

Blockbuster offseason addition Myles Garrett failed to record a tackle or sack in his Rams debut. Garrett was eventually placed on injured reserve due to arthroscopic knee surgery, sidelining him for a minimum of four games.

While Donald has been away from the NFL for multiple years, it isn't difficult to imagine him making his presence felt once he takes the field again.

After all, he remained productive throughout his last season with Los Angeles in 2023. In 16 games that year, Donald racked up 53 tackles, 23 quarterback hits, 16 tackles for loss, eight sacks and three passes defended.

The Rams will be facing a Giants offensive line that allowed just two sacks in a 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1.

Kickoff between Los Angeles and New York is on Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 'F--king Move the Ball,' Packers Center Talks Game Plan vs. Jets, Need to 'Protect' Jordan Love
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers center Sean Rhyan has quite the game plan for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers center Sean Rhyan has quite the game plan for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.

"F--king protect J-Love and f--king move the ball," he told reporters when asked about the team's plans. "Keep it simple, keep it easy."

Protecting Jordan Love was a significant problem in Green Bay's Week 1 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

The Vikings sacked him four times and tallied six quarterback hits while relentlessly blitzing throughout the game. Love still managed to throw for 387 yards and two touchdowns, but he also threw an interception and fumbled twice, losing one of them.

Minnesota's defense eventually overwhelmed the Packers offensive line and Love in the process, as the visitors managed just three points after halftime.

That opened the door for the Vikings to overcome a 22-10 deficit on the way to a commanding 39-22 victory. Even with Kyler Murray sidelined, quarterback Carson Wentz made enough plays on the other end while the defense seized momentum with its pressure on Love.

While no longer having to face defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his tendency to blitz figures to be a break for Rhyan and the rest of the Green Bay offensive line, the Jets impressed on the defensive side during their 23-10 season-opening win over the Tennessee Titans.

New York sacked Cam Ward three times and finished with five quarterback hits. The Titans didn't find the end zone until the fourth quarter, and even that touchdown came in garbage time while they were trailing by 20 points.

A Packers offensive line that failed to give Love enough time to throw throughout the second half of their first loss will have to be much better against the Jets. If they aren't, Green Bay could be staring at an 0-2 record to start the season.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Responds to Cowboys' Doubters After Loss to Giants, 'Nobody's More Pissed Than Myself'
articles.summary: Dak Prescott provided his response to doubters of the Dallas Cowboys following the team's 28-20 defeat at the hands of the New York Giants in Week 1.
articles.body:
Dak Prescott provided his response to doubters of the Dallas Cowboys following the team's 28-20 defeat at the hands of the New York Giants in Week 1.

"I mean, it's a long season," Prescott told reporters Thursday. "I love our fans, but I don't necessarily feel like I need to speak to that fan. Sorry for them. If they're a real fan, they'll stick with it. They'll trust it. They'll believe in it. And at the end of the day, it is one game. Yeah, it sucks, it's the first game.

"Nobody's more pissed than myself and these guys in here. We didn't want to start 0-1. We're as excited as any fan out there about the offseason and things we've done in the training camp. So, turn that energy and come to the game this Sunday and be as loud as you can. We appreciate it."

After consecutive seven-win seasons in 2024 and 2025, the Cowboys revamped their defense heading into their 2026 campaign.

They added pass-rusher Rashan Gary to a defensive line that already featured Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark before bolstering their secondary by signing safety Jalen Thompson in free agency. Dallas also selected safety Caleb Downs with the No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft.

Still, the Cowboys experienced issues slowing down the Giants in Week 1.

New York finished with 394 total yards and 29 first downs, punting on just one of its seven drives. The Giants were also able to control the clock throughout the second half, as the Cowboys only had two possessions across the final two quarters of action.

As for Prescott, he went 22-of-34 for 175 yards and two touchdowns compared to one interception.

It isn't hard to imagine the veteran passer bouncing back, as he's coming off a 2025 campaign in which he threw for 4,552 yards and 30 touchdowns. There are still concerns surrounding Dallas' defense, though.

The Cowboys will attempt to avoid an 0-2 start against NFC East rivals during a Week 2 matchup with the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Kickoff is at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. listed with back issue again a day after Steelers changed his designation to 'non-injury/conditioning'
articles.summary: Porter reportedly left the field Thursday with a member of Pittsburgh's medical staff during the portion of practice open to media.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers changed Joey Porter Jr.'s injury report designation to "non-injury/conditioning" on Wednesday. Before Steelers practice on Thursday, head coach Mike McCarthy was asked if that update meant the cornerback's lingering back injury was resolved.

"I've never spoke on the back," said McCarthy , who noted earlier in his news conference that Porter was scheduled to do more Thursday than he did as a limited participant Wednesday.

But Porter — notably still embroiled in a longstanding contract dispute with the organization — was again limited on Thursday, and this time his "back" designation resurfaced on the injury report.

The 26-year-old corner left the field with a member of Pittsburgh's medical staff during the portion of practice open to media, according to multiple reports Thursday .

It was reported this summer that Porter aggravated his back injury during a mobility workout on the first day of training camp. That landed him on the physically unable to perform list. In the lead-up to the season opener, which the Steelers won 20-13 against the Atlanta Falcons , Porter was activated off the PUP list.

Even so, it was uncertain if Porter would play in Week 1. McCarthy cited the necessary ramp-up needed in the return-to-play process. Meanwhile, Porter's contentious contract situation loomed, with the Steelers adhering to their to their policy of not continuing negotiations into the regular season.

While Porter clearly has the support of teammates — fellow cornerback Jalen Ramsey said last month, "They've got to pay Joey Porter," per The Athletic — the ongoing standoff between Porter and the franchise has sparked debate about potential trade scenarios .

Porter is a key ingredient for Pittsburgh's defense. The son of Super Bowl-winning Steelers linebacker Joey Porter, the Penn State product turned in an impressive 2025 campaign. He allowed only 29 receptions and 299 receiving yards on 60 targets, according to Pro Football Focus, which has him with just one receiving touchdown allowed across three seasons in the league. Additionally, Porter piled up a career-high 14 passes defended last season, per Pro Football Reference.

Porter is due for a pay raise . The cornerback market was reset this offseason, with New England Patriots standout Christian Gonzalez receiving a four-year, $135 million extension that made him the highest-paid corner in NFL history . He leads all players at the position with an average annual value of $33.8 million, per Over the Cap .

articles.title: Inspiring story on second chances: "It wasn't easy for me. It was tough. I got my scholarship taken from me"-How Travis Kelce overcame a career setback to become an NFL superstar
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s path to NFL stardom did not begin with a smooth rise. Before the Super Bowl celebrations, record-breaking catches and Kansas City spotl.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s path to NFL stardom did not begin with a smooth rise. Before the Super Bowl celebrations, record-breaking catches and Kansas City spotlight, he faced a major setback at the University of Cincinnati that cost him his scholarship and his place on the football team. His own recollections reveal how that difficult period became a turning point in his career.Travis Kelce’s Cincinnati setback changed his football journeyKelce arrived at Cincinnati as a talented quarterback prospect, but his college career took an unexpected turn after the 2009 season. Following a failed marijuana test before the 2010 Sugar Bowl, he was suspended for the 2010 season and lost his scholarship.Suddenly, the football career he had been building was no longer guaranteed.Kelce later spoke openly about that period while being inducted into the Cleveland Heights High School Hall of Fame with his brother, Jason. Rather than glossing over the mistakes, he acknowledged exactly where he stood at the time.“It’s not because I don’t appreciate the time I had at the University of Cincinnati, because I do, I cherish it dearly. But there was a time when I was at Cincinnati that it wasn't easy for me. It was tough. I got my scholarship taken from me. I did a lot of dumb things. I'm sure a lot of people in this room know someone from Heights that's done a lot of dumb things. To all my friends, I was that guy.”That admission gives a different perspective on Kelce’s eventual success. His breakthrough did not come simply because he was talented. He first had to repair the damage he had caused and earn another opportunity.Without his scholarship, Kelce moved in with Jason and took a telemarketing job. ESPN reported that he earned $8 an hour while making calls and dealing with frustrated customers. For someone accustomed to spending his life playing sports, the experience was a major adjustment.Travis Kelce found motivation during his lowest pointThe difficult period also forced Kelce to think differently about what he wanted from his future.Looking back on his telemarketing job, he explained how unfamiliar that life felt to him.“All I had been doing is playing outside, playing sports my entire life. I had never sat down and tried to earn a living like that. That's not to hit on anybody's 9-to-5; that's just not for me.”Then came the realisation that he still had a route back to football.“The light at the end of the tunnel was that if I do what I'm supposed to do instead of being a knucklehead, I can have a way better life than this.”That mindset became important. Cincinnati gave Kelce a path back, but reinstatement did not simply erase what had happened. He had to demonstrate that he could handle the opportunity.The university has since described how Kelce worked his way back onto the team and eventually earned his scholarship again before his breakout senior season in 2012.Kelce has credited the people around him for believing he could change.“The players, the coaches, the staff that was at the university at the time – really believed in me to be able to turn things around and do better for myself. That was huge for me at the time.”That second chance also came with a major change on the field. Kelce had been recruited as a quarterback, but he switched to tight end as part of his return to the team. He later explained that Cincinnati needed help at the position and that his athletic ability could translate well there.Jason Kelce’s support mattered when Travis needed itTravis’ comeback was also closely tied to his relationship with Jason.When Travis lost his scholarship and housing, Jason provided him with a place to stay. The brothers shared a room while Travis worked his way back into football.That support went beyond simply giving his younger brother a roof over his head. Travis has repeatedly acknowledged the role Jason played during one of the most uncertain periods of his life.At Cincinnati, the opportunity to return eventually changed the direction of his career. Travis later explained that earning his scholarship back helped him mature and understand the value of discipline.“I was fortunate that the football team was able to give me the opportunity to work back into to trying to get a scholarship that I was able to get by the time my senior year came around. It helped me mature a lot. It let me know I could have a lot of happiness if I do some things like go to class and try my best to be a professional at the college level.”His senior season provided the next step. After rebuilding his standing at Cincinnati, Kelce entered the 2013 NFL Draft and was selected by the Kansas City Chiefs in the third round. His journey from a suspended college player to an NFL draft pick had taken only a few years, but the road between those points changed him.From second chance to Travis Kelce’s NFL legacyKelce eventually developed into one of the defining tight ends of his generation, but the foundation for that career was laid before his NFL debut.His Cincinnati setback remains an important part of his story because Kelce himself has never presented his journey as perfect. Instead, he has spoken about making mistakes, receiving another opportunity and understanding what he needed to do with it.That is also why his comments about Cincinnati remain significant years later. He has expressed gratitude toward the coaches, staff and teammates who helped him rebuild his career.The lesson in Kelce’s story is not that setbacks automatically lead to success. His return required accountability, another opportunity and sustained work after he received it. Cincinnati gave him a route back, while Kelce had to make the most of it.By the time Kansas City selected him in 2013, the player who had once lost his scholarship had already learned what it meant to fight for another chance.His later NFL success made the contrast even sharper. But the most revealing part of the story may be what Kelce said about the difficult period itself. He did not hide from the mistakes that put his career at risk. He acknowledged them, accepted the consequences and used the opportunity he received to change the direction of his life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Christian Parker is on to Week 2 after a rough debut as defensive coordinator of the Cowboys
articles.summary: New Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker didn't have to wait long for a tense sideline exchange to end up on social media, or for the duty to try to...
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas (AP) — New Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker didn't have to wait long for a tense sideline exchange to end up on social media, or for the duty to try to explain a poor performance that has become all too familiar for fans of the Cowboys.

Parker got his first chance to call defensive plays as a 34-year-old because the Cowboys fired Matt Eberflus after his only season when he oversaw one of the worst defenses in the NFL, and in franchise history.

Following an offseason and training camp filled with optimism over a young coach and a revamped roster, the Cowboys looked frighteningly similar to 2025 in a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants in the opener.

The defense wasn't very good in the first half, and even worse in the second, when the Giants scored touchdowns on eight-minute drives on their first two possessions and ran out the clock on the third. Dallas scored TDs the only two times it got the ball after the break.

Somewhere amid all that, Parker was caught on camera in a sideline exchange with rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham , who always has an intense look and in this case started barking back at Parker from the bench before getting up and storming off.

It's safe to say it was a rough debut for both — Barham as an NFL player and Parker as an NFL play-caller.

"He was a little frustrated with himself and frustrated with our side of the ball," Parker said. "But I don't think anybody in our building has any doubt of what he's going to do coming real soon. We don't have any reservations about his mentality. We welcome that passion. Have to channel it better. And that's something that young players have to go through. It's a natural progression. We have a lot of confidence in Jaishawn."

Coach Brian Schottenheimer, in his second season in charge after 25 years as an NFL assistant, isn't losing confidence in Parker after one week. Dallas is home against Washington in a matchup of 0-1 teams Sunday.

"I have no question Christian Parker is the right guy for this job," Schottenheimer said. "He will learn from this, just like our young players are going to learn from this. We're going to play our young players this weekend too, and they're going to play better and Christian's going to call a better game this week and feel better about it."

The Cowboys added two veteran pass rushers in Rashan Gary and Von Miller , and Barham was among the reasons for optimism when the third-round pick emerged as a potential starter during the preseason.

Caleb Downs was the 12th overall pick as a safety, and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence was the other first-rounder for Dallas at No. 23.

There was reason to believe the run defense could be stout anchored by defensive tackles Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark .

Instead, the Cowboys didn't offer much resistance against Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo , and the secondary left huge gaps in coverage the same way Dallas did a season ago.

Parker is aware of all those things, and was reserved and measured the first time he had to face the questions that come with such a dismal showing.

"It's one poor performance," Parker said. "It's one loss that does not equal two. I think we're not trying to make excuses for anything. We're not trying to act like it didn't happen. We got to look in the mirror, we got to be accountable for what we did wrong and what we did right, correct it and then move on to the next opponent because it can't be a hangover and it can't linger."

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs held tryouts for four linebackers on Thursday
articles.summary: According to reports, the Kansas City Chiefs held tryouts for four linebackers on Thursday | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
The recent injury to Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Cooper McDonald will keep him out of action for at least four games after he was placed on injured reserve Wednesday. The front office is already focusing on potentially adding a new player to the roster at that position.

According to A to Z Sports' Charles Goldman, the Chiefs hosted free agent linebackers Marte Mapu , Dominic DeLuca, Langston Patterson, and TJ Quinn for tryouts on Thursday.

DeLuca, Patterson, and Quinn are undrafted free agents from the 2026 NFL Draft class who were unable to make their initial training camp squad's 53-man roster. Mapu has the most experience and was selected by the New England Patriots in the third round (76th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. He notably had his first career interception against Patrick Mahomes in Week 15 of his rookie season.

After three seasons in New England , the Houston Texans traded for Mapu in 2026. He was later waived/injured on August 24, before being officially released the next day. In 2025, he recorded 25 total tackles, one forced fumble, and one interception. The former Sacramento State standout is 26 and has significant NFL linebacker experience.

articles.title: Watch Josh Allen Score Historic 1st TD at New Highmark Stadium on Video During Debut Game
articles.summary: It's only fitting the first regular-season touchdown in Highmark Stadium belongs to Josh Allen.
articles.body:
It's only fitting the first regular-season touchdown in Highmark Stadium belongs to Josh Allen.

The Buffalo Bills quarterback led his team on an 85-yard drive on the first possession of Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions and capped it off with a one-yard touchdown run. It was his 82nd career rushing touchdown, which tied Corey Dillon for 19th in NFL history.

ESPN noted Highmark Stadium cost more than $2.1 billion with a capacity of more than 60,000.

It also features "specific features to combat the Buffalo weather," including underground heating coils to prevent the natural-grass field from freezing and a 360-degree canopy covering approximately 60 percent of the seating bowl.

While the new stadium generated plenty of attention for Thursday's debut, Allen is always the center of attention in Buffalo.

The franchise icon is arguably the best quarterback in the NFL and took home the 2024 MVP. He has four seasons with more than 4,000 passing yards and has led the Bills to the playoffs in each of the last seven years.

If the start of Thursday's game was any indication, he's going to put up some impressive numbers in the new stadium as well.

articles.title: Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson explains siding with family over DCF in custody dispute involving gender identity

articles.title: Believe the hype: Giants' bully ball, Ben Johnson's offense and 4 others who aren't going away this NFL season
articles.summary: I highlighted a half-dozen units and players that made a strong Week 1 impression, and explain why we need to keep eyeballs on them throughout the season.
articles.body:
Week 1 is firmly behind us, but the reactions (and overreactions ) are still reverberating as we approach Week 2. And what's more fun than to act like Disco Stu pointing at a graph of disco sales going up forever and extrapolate the first showings of NFL teams in this young 2026 season?

I highlighted a half-dozen units and players that made a strong first step in Week 1, and explain why we need to keep eyeballs on them throughout the season.

Offenses in the Big Apple (or Big Apple adjacent)

I had an inkling that the Jets would have more competence to them in 2026, even if I wasn't quite sure what that might look like.

Well, apparently it'll look like a bevy of tight ends and a burly, well-coached, and just straight physical run game. Geno Smith , who had cleaner pockets to work from in Week 1 than he did in his recent experiences in Las Vegas and Seattle , launched throws downfield and to the outside to create space in the offense.

Kenyon Sadiq was used in creative ways, including a jet sweep for a touchdown and a package that featured 14 personnel (1 RB, 4 TEs, 0 WRs. The running back was actually fullback Andrew Beck ) and Sadiq in the backfield as a running back.

The Jets' passing attack used concepts like "Flood" to overload the Titans' defense, a positive sign that offensive coordinator Frank Reich is aware of how to attack a defense in 2026.

Mason Taylor looks like a strong starter as an in-line tight end who can block and provide receiving value. The offensive line features a star in Armand Membou at right tackle and Olu Fashanu looking way better without quarterbacks behind him creating their own pressure. And there is enough juice at wide receiver and running back ( Breece Hall and Braelon Allen were strong runners Sunday) that there is a high ceiling of explosive plays in this offense.

Yes, it's the Titans. But the Jets completely outclassed them in Week 1. I'm looking forward to checking on this offense and the stuff Reich has in store every week.

The Giants, too, showed off their bully ball offense in the season opener, completely steamrolling the Cowboys' defense with heavy personnel and Cam Skattebo treating every tackle attempt like an insult.

Pat Ricard led the way on plenty of runs behind the Giants' talented offensive line. Francis Mauigoa had a good showing in his first NFL action at right guard, along with the strong tackle pairing of Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor .

I was impressed by the Giants' auxiliary blockers at the skill positions, too. Isaiah Likely caught the passes, but the other Giants tight ends showed up to set the edge and create space for the running backs to pick their spots. And rookie Malachi Fields , one of the best blocking prospects in this year's wide receiver class, picked up where he left off in college, providing several crack blocks on the edge and the willingness and ability to insert inside.

The Giants put together four drives of 10 or more plays against the Cowboys. The early-down success led to more tolerable third-down distances, and Jaxson Dart played his most efficient (and calm) game of his young career. The Giants went 9-for-10 on third down before taking a knee on their final drive.

The Giants' passing game had a good showing and will still need to pass the test in less favorable game scripts, but their offense, and better coached defense with Abdul Carter emerging as a star, will make them a tough out against teams not prepared to buckle up their chinstraps for 60 minutes.

And, wouldn't you know it, the Giants' Week 2 opponent, the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams, had issues in 2025 against heavier personnel groupings. L.A. allowed 5.9 yards per play on early downs against offenses with two or fewer wide receivers.

Let's see if the Giants can deflate the football again and control the game script against a defense now without Myles Garrett .

Big "they played the Browns" caveat here.

But wow the Jaguars' offense, and Trevor Lawrence , looked excellent in Week 1. Lawrence finished with the second-best single-game success rate of his NFL career (a whopping 68%, per TruMedia). Lawrence was constantly getting the ball out on one hitch, while still pushing the ball over 10 air yards per pass attempt. His offensive line looked like it got a boost with Anton Harrison moving to the left side and rookie Emmanuel Pregnon slotting next to him at left guard.

The Jaguars are deep at pass catcher, with a fun mix of skill sets, too. Even rookie sixth-rounder Josh Cameron showed up as a blocker and made a great catch on one of the tightest-window throws you'll ever see from Lawrence for a touchdown.

There's even the ability for this offense to pivot when it needs to get bigger bodies on the field. Nate Boerkircher had a good showing as an in-line blocker and new addition Chris Rodriguez brings a much needed thumper to this run game to keep the Jaguars on track. Boerkircher and Rodriguez are perfect complements to Brenton Strange (a dynamic pass catcher and no slouch as a blocker in his own right) and the explosive Bhayshul Tuten .

Liam Coen and his offensive staff have shown they can dial up plays with the best of them, and Lawrence has never played with more confidence. The offensive line isn't a top-end unit, but it has enough to be above board, and a coaching staff that knows how to work around the group.

The Jaguars have a great test in front of them, traveling to Denver in Week 2 to face a Broncos defense that I'm sure will be geared up after chasing Kenneth Walker all over the field on Monday night.

The Chiefs invested in Walker and it looks like a run-first philosophy this season (which was encouraging to see) . Even Emmett Johnson had some strong touches in his first NFL regular-season action.

What was also encouraging was just how fast the Chiefs' defense looked. Nohl Williams is emerging as the next star cornerback to graduate from the School of Spags. Mansoor Delane looked great in the preseason and came down with an interception on the first third down of the season before bowing out with a shoulder injury. Peter Woods and R Mason Thomas injected some much needed juice into this front, alleviating the attention (and overall snaps played) by Chris Jones . Even returnee L'Jarius Sneed appears to have shored up the slot position for the Chiefs and allows the other defensive backs to play on the backend.

All in all, it was a great showing from the Chiefs' revamped running game and defense. And I think the defense has all the makings of a top-10 unit already, that should get only better as its young players play more.

More specifically, Coker as an outside wide receiver.

Coker has already shown off his strength and QB-friendly route running when operating as a power slot in his young career with the Carolina Panthers . But, beginning with the end of last year, Coker's work from the outside has him rising up in just where I stack him among the league's pass catchers.

Coker ran 19 routes against the Bears when aligned as an outside wide receiver, the most of his NFL career, per NextGenStats; 59.4% of his routes came from the outside, a huge jump when compared to his career rates that hovered around 37%.

And it's not just alignment, it's how he produced on the outside, too. Coker finished with 5 receptions on 5 targets for 108 yards and 2 touchdowns when aligned on the outside against the Bears. That yardage doubled his previous career-best single-game total.

Coker and Tetairoa McMillan make for a strong (and large) 1-2 punch at wide receiver. With both able to operate on the inside and outside and with huge catching ranges that look like the Vitruvian Man drawing. They're paired with a solid group of tight ends in Tommy Tremble , Mitchell Evans and Darren Waller . And it's an interesting group of big bodies for Bryce Young to throw to (Young also had an encouraging Week 1 against the Bears' iffy defense).

The Panthers' defense appears to have more work to do, but it was a good showing from Carolina's young offense, especially their former undrafted, and recently extended, wide receiver.

I mean, 59 points. And that's with a turnover and getting stopped on fourth down, too. The run game looked great. Every single skill player showed a willingness to block and open up opportunities for their teammates. The offensive line looked in midseason form despite a couple of new faces at left tackle and center. ( Braxton Jones played well at left tackle. Garrett Bradbury remains the weak link of this group, though).

Caleb Williams looked calm in the pocket, and has already shown improved timing on his passes and willingness to work over the middle. There's the added bonus of Williams being one of the best creators and playmakers when things go askew.

Ben Johnson's offense was clicking on all cylinders, and the designs in the run game and play-action concepts off of them are top-tier stuff.

From the big plays, like creating an I formation run out of 11 personnel, showing an awareness on how to manipulate the Panthers' defense:

To even shorter gains showing off interesting change-ups for defenses to deal with, like this wind-back run concept in the red zone:

Johnson says he wants to set the points record this season. 59 points, the second-most ever by an NFL offense in Week 1, is a big first step toward being one of those offenses that gets slapped with a nickname when it's all said and done. We might have to start workshopping a couple.

articles.title: NFL Fans React to Josh Allen, Jared Goff, Gibbs, Cook, St. Brown Fantasy Performances in Bills-Lions
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills came out firing on all cylinders in their first game in New Highmark Stadium on Thursday.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills came out firing on all cylinders in their first game in New Highmark Stadium on Thursday.

The Bills were nearly perfect in the first half against the Detroit Lions, taking a 27-10 lead into the third quarter behind a tremendous offensive showing.

Allen threw for 164 yards and three touchdowns in the first half, finding Dalton Kincaid, Josh Palmer and Dawson Knox in the end zone. Allen added 40 rushing yards and another score, and Bills running back James Cook torched the Lions' defense with 101 rushing yards.

The Lions' offense was a completely different story. Jared Goff had 128 passing yards and a touchdown in the first half, and Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 47 yards. Star receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown didn't do much either, getting just two receptions for 33 yards.

The polar opposite first half from the two teams saw fantasy managers with Allen rejoice, while those who have Goff lamented Detroit's struggles.

The Bills' offensive showing was impressive, but far from surprising given what they've done with Allen under center in the past.

The Lions, meanwhile, showed that they still have plenty of room for improvement on both sides of the ball.

articles.title: DJ Moore Injured, Latest News on Bills WR's Status and Fantasy Implications After Exiting vs. Lions
articles.summary: Almost everything went right for the Buffalo Bills and fantasy managers with their players during the first half of Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions except when it came to wide receiver DJ Moore.
articles.body:
Almost everything went right for the Buffalo Bills and fantasy managers with their players during the first half of Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions except when it came to wide receiver DJ Moore.

The Bills announced Moore was ruled out with a shoulder injury after he was taken to the locker room for X-rays. He suffered the injury when he was going for a pass in the first half and before the Bills took a 27-10 lead into intermission.

Buffalo added Moore from the Chicago Bears via trade this offseason as one of its major roster changes heading into the new campaign.

Moore has four seasons with more than 1,000 receiving yards on his resume, and he is also someone who figured to provide veteran leadership for the receiving room. And it was a receiving room that could use more firepower.

For as excellent as Buffalo's offense is with Josh Allen leading the way, Khalil Shakir was the only wide receiver on the team who reached the 500-yard mark last year. Even he wasn't completely dominant with 719 receiving yards, underscoring the need for a game-changing receiver on the roster to unlock the Super Bowl ceiling.

Moore figured to be that game-changing receiver, and he was in the season opener against the Houston Texans with five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown.

Fortunately for Buffalo, Thursday's game is just Week 2. That gives Moore a significant amount of time to ideally get back into the lineup before the stretch run for the Bills.

As for fantasy football, this is an opportunity for some of the Bills' other pass-catchers to put up numbers in the immediate future. Shakir is someone who should be in lineups as long as Moore isn't, while players such as Joshua Palmer and Keon Coleman are at least worth consideration.

The tight end is arguably Allen's top option in the aerial attack with Moore sidelined. He just finished with five catches for 130 yards against the Texans and scored a touchdown in the first half of Thursday's game against the Lions.

Still, the Bills will be far more dangerous in the AFC with Moore on the field.

articles.title: Watch Fernando Mendoza Star in Funny New State Farm Video After Raiders No. 1 Draft Pick
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza starred in a comedic State Farm commercial as he begins his rookie season.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza starred in a comedic State Farm commercial as he begins his rookie season.

In the new commercial, Mendoza worries about Las Vegas being a negative influence on him while speaking to Jake from State Farm. The signal-caller then completes a series of activities including eating a cookie after brushing his teeth and saying "Go fish" while playing blackjack.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft is known for his wholesome demeanor and previously explained why he didn't experience the Las Vegas Strip after joining the Raiders.

"I've been there once or twice, but I haven't really experienced the Strip," Mendoza told Michael Silver of The Athletic during training camp. "It's like a boogeyman. A lot of people talk about the Strip like, 'You don't want to go there.'

"It's like when you're a kid; you're trick-or-treating, and there's the haunted house. You're not trying to go over there."

After a 2025 season at Indiana in which Mendoza earned Heisman Trophy honors and won a national championship, he's started his 2026 campaign as Las Vegas' No. 2 quarterback behind veteran Kirk Cousins.

The Raiders opened the year with a 1-0 record following a season-opening 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday.

articles.title: Bills Beat Lions, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Josh Allen, Gibbs, Goff, Cook, Top Players
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills established themselves as Super Bowl candidates in Week 1, and they did nothing to dispel that notion in Week 2.
articles.body:
Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills established themselves as Super Bowl candidates in Week 1, and they did nothing to dispel that notion in Week 2.

In their first game in the New Highmark Stadium, the Bills beat the Detroit Lions 41-31.

What's more, Bills head coach Joe Brady became the first head coach in franchise history to start his coaching career 2-0.

The Bills came in as 5.5-point favorites (via FanDuel Sportsbook ) after a strong showing against the Houston Texans to start the season.

The Bills could do no wrong in the first half, quickly jumping out to a 27-7 lead thanks to a rushing touchdown from Allen plus touchdown catches from Joshua Palmer, Dawson Knox and Dalton Kincaid.

The Lions had a slow first half but managed to gain some momentum in the third quarter with a touchdown from Amon-Ra St. Brown to start the second half, but Buffalo answered quickly to jump back out to a 34-17 lead.

Jared Goff's touchdown pass to Sam LaPorta early in the fourth quarter kept Detroit alive, and the Lions forced a Bills punt on the following drive. Things stalled after a quick three-and-out, though.

From there, the Bills mounted a lengthy clock-killing drive that ended with a James Cook touchdown. Detroit answered with a score to make it a 10-point game, but had far too little time to mount a comeback.

For Bills fans, it's hard not to feel good about how Buffalo has looked through the first two weeks of the season. Allen appears to be on his way to another MVP-caliber season, and he has some solid weapons around him.

The Bills' defense has room for improvement, but it's been an otherwise perfect start to the year.

The Lions went to overtime with a rebuilding New Orleans Saints squad in Week 1 before the double-digit loss on Thursday, so they have some reflecting to do as they try to make their way back to the playoffs.

articles.title: Lions' defense could be their fatal flaw again
articles.summary: The Lions' defense is in rough shape right now. They scored 31 points and never had a chance against the Bills.
articles.body:
The Lions have a problem on defense, and it's becoming one that their high-powered offense can't overcome.

The Bills stormed out to a 21-point first-half lead and held off the Lions, 41-31, on Thursday night . Buffalo racked up nearly 300 yards of offense by halftime, as Josh Allen and James Cook carved up the Lions all night. They were largely without top wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) and still faced little resistance all night.

To the Lions' credit, they kept pushing the pedal offensively, three times fighting back to make it a 10-point game in the second half, but they came up short.

The Bills went for blood right away, efficiently moving downfield in an explosive first quarter. Lions penalties wiped out a red-zone fumble and sack on back-to-back plays, and the Bills made them pay by punching it in and making it a three-touchdown lead.

The Lions moved the ball Thursday, but they couldn't stop it. The Bills finished 9-for-11 on third downs and scored on all five of their red-zone trips. Even for a short-week road game against an elite offense, it was a long night for the Lions' defense.

It was telling when head coach Dan Campbell put the spotlight on his offense after the Lions nearly blew a 21-0 lead. It feels like Campbell understands his team's reality.

If the Lions are not on point offensively from the start, they risk falling in too big a hole. If they fail to put a team away, as they almost did in Week 1, the Lions can let a game they were dominating slip away.

The defense has been the Lions' downfall the past few seasons. The way things are shaping up, it appears to be their Achilles heel again.

Detroit 's secondary was in tough shape heading into Thursday's game. D.J. Reed (foot) started, but he and Rock Ya-Sin have been under fire early this season. The depth has been thinned considerably with Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) on PUP and after waiving Terrion Arnold . Making matters worse, replacement starter Avonte Maddox left Thursday's game with a foot injury.

The Lions started Week 1 on fire defensively, blanking the Saints on their first eight possessions and forcing three turnovers. Then New Orleans scored 30 points on its next six series, with a missed field goal its only empty possession.

From that point on, through Thursday, the Lions have been a sieve defensively. The Bills scored four straight touchdowns to open the game, punted once, then scored touchdowns on two of their next three possessions.

That's 10 touchdowns allowed in their past 80 minutes of football. The question is how it'll get better.

How much defensive hope is there in Detroit?

Branch appears poised for a return in October, which is good news. The forecast on Joseph is less clear. But safety is not the biggest concern — cornerback is. The Lions just can't cover efficiently against high-powered passing games.

Could they try to pry Joey Porter Jr. out of Pittsburgh ? More realistically, they might have to hope former second-rounder Ennis Rakestraw Jr. can work his way back into the lineup. But one way or another, the Lions must upgrade at secondary — or find ways to crank up the pass rush to help mask their back-end issues.

Aidan Hutchinson is off to a hot start, with two sacks in Week 1 and two more Thursday. Derrick Barnes also has made big plays in both games. They're trying. But the front seven hasn't dominated enough to offset the coverage.

To this point, general manager Brad Holmes hasn't quite solved the puzzle of how to field a capable defense with his explosive offense. The Lions overlooked safety in the draft, despite knowing about the Branch and Joseph injuries, and the cornerback room is somehow thinner, even if the Arnold situation can hardly be held too hard against Holmes.

Still, the problem is real. Holmes has built a roster that's very strong almost everywhere but the unit is currently holding the Lions back, and there were opportunities to add help prior to Week 1. It won't be easy to find solutions this season to this multi-issue, multi-year problem — not now anyway.

They have a few manageable games coming up, plus an early bye in Week 6. But time won't heal all their issues.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Week 2 Top Takeaways and Biggest Questions for Every Team
articles.summary: Fireworks for the NFL's second week of action began early when the visiting Detroit Lions helped christen the Buffalo Bills' brand new Highmark Stadium.
articles.body:
Fireworks for the NFL's second week of action began early when the visiting Detroit Lions helped christen the Buffalo Bills' brand new Highmark Stadium.

The marquee match followed Sunday's blistering performances, where last weekend's outcomes made it the highest-scoring Week 1 Sunday in NFL history. The rest of the teams around the league also hope to register high marks as they work their way through Week 2.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the action to break down each contest, provide takeaways and ask the most pressing questions.

Dalton Kincaid Is Buffalo Bills' No. 1 Target Special tight ends aren't just weapons in their respective offenses; they can be No. 1 options in the passing game. Dalton Kincaid should be officially anointed as the Bills' top receiving threat after the first two weeks of play. The tight end caught a team-leading seven catches Thursday for 95 yards and a touchdown. He now has 12 grabs for 225 yards after facing the Houston Texans and Detroit. Kincaid's emergence helps soften the blow of DJ Moore leaving the Week 2 contest with a shoulder injury. The Bills traded for Moore this offseason to be their WR1. Without him in the lineup for any period of time, Buffalo is back where it started at wide receiver. Instead, quarterback Josh Allen can continually lean on Kincaid, who's usage could mirror that of a Travis Kelce or George Kittle. Bills' Greg Rousseau Evolves Into Final Form In a world enamored by Pokemon, Rousseau has made the transition from beginner Charmander to a full-blown Charizard, and he's been on a heater to start the 2026 campaign. The 2021 first-round draft pick has been flying off the edge and creating havoc everywhere. He followed his two-sack performance in Week 1 with another pair of sacks against the Lions. He also has nine quarterback hits during that stretch. This caliber of play could eventually warrant national recognition. For now, the Bills should be content with the emerging difference-maker, because Rousseau's four sacks so far are only three behind last season's team-leading output.

Detroit's Dismal Defense Dooms Docket The Lions expected a bounce-back campaign this fall. Detroit won't come close to the team that made an NFC Championship Game appearance during the 2024 campaign if its defense isn't fixed. During Thursday's contest, the Buffalo Bills accumulated 446 total yards and scored 34 points before the fourth quarter even began. The Lions' pitiful defensive effort came on the heels of nearly surrendering a 21-point second-half lead to the New Orleans Saints four days earlier. The Saints managed 469 yards during that contest. The Lions didn't own the NFL's worst defense coming out of Week 1, but back-to-back weeks of inferior performances offset anything Detroit does offensively. Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs' Play Deserves Attention Detroit has a lot to fix after its 1-1 start. Whereas Gibbs has been a silver (and Honolulu blue) lining. The Lions' running back managed 113 yards from scrimmage Thursday. He's a legitimate weapon in both phases of the game and nearly impossible for any defense to guard. Amon-Ra St. Brown provides high-end consistency as a pass-catcher. However, Gibbs' explosive traits and ability to create mismatches elevates the entire offense. If the Lions can't slow any opponent defensively, Gibbs is the caliber of player who can still keep Detroit in games.

A season can get out of hand quickly. This Sunday's setup may be a perfect example of how organizations can head in drastically different directions even this early in the process.

articles.title: As Cowboys' defense is reminded NFL 'isn’t a fairy tale,' DC Christian Parker holds himself accountable first
articles.summary: Parker has adjusted some of his weekly schedule based off the opener. He placed extra emphasis on signals and eye contact in anticipation of a loud home crow...
articles.body:
As Christian Parker stood before the Cowboys' defense this week, Dallas ' first-year defensive coordinator cycled through his unit's errors.

Parker showed his players where they lost leverage and he showed them when their eyes were focused toward the wrong place. Parker cued up block destruction weaknesses during their 28-20 loss to the New York Giants , and he acknowledged the moments communication broke down.

But first and foremost on the list of what Dallas' defense agreed were "fixable mistakes," Parker acknowledged his own play-calling regrets.

"Everybody was accountable — including me," Parker said Thursday. "I showed them the plays I was referencing that I didn't feel great about. … There are a couple plays I certainly wish I had back, for different reasons.

"I think that'll be the case, win or loss, any game."

Parker's decision to explain aloud the play calls he now sees differently from the heat of the moment follows a pattern the 34-year-old has established since the Cowboys hired him in January to transform Dallas' defense from a 4-3 (four defensive linemen, three linebackers) base unit to a 3-4 base unit (three defensive linemen, four linebackers) for the first time in 14 years.

Dallas' dead-last scoring defense last year reflected some dearth of talent after the club traded edge rusher Micah Parsons one week before its season opener. But the weekly gashes the Cowboys absorbed also reflected a troubling pattern of miscommunications that Parker was hired to remedy.

"His biggest thing, and I think you'll see it out here, is he is so into communication," executive vice president Stephen Jones told Yahoo Sports during training camp. "The communication is huge amongst the players. I think we lacked a lot of that last year in terms of communication."

The Cowboys lacked it also in their season opener — perhaps not unrelated to the loss by injury of veteran safety Malik Hooker and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , the latter wearing the "green dot" radio to communicate Cowboys' defensive play calls from Parker to his teammates before a hamstring injury.

Neither Parker nor his colleagues are downplaying the concerns from Week 1, Parker insisting "we're not trying to make excuses for anything and we're not trying to act like it didn't happen."

But as the Cowboys allowed 394 yards (seventh-worst) and an 81.82% third-down completion rate (worst among defenses in Week 1), they believe they're in control of the solution: communicating their way out of miscommunications.

"Any clean play that happens, I think, where we execute and everybody's on the same page, there was some level or form of communication or confirmation that occurred that allowed us to do that," Parker told Yahoo Sports during a training camp interview. "Tape is silent. So you want to see verbal communication and nonverbal communication on tape. You can see the body language with it and then you get that confirmation in the meeting room."

Against the Washington Commanders , Parker won't be looking for only splash plays. He'll be looking for disciplined fundamentals.

"The most routine plays," he said, "are the ones that make me the happiest."

'If you don't work at it, you're going to suck at it'

During training camp, Cowboys defensive meetings were borderline boisterous.

Coaches and players and then more coaches and more players were talking. That was by design.

Parker, a graduate of the University of Richmond, learned from his small undergraduate classes the value of discussion and participation. He settled that when he became the head of a position group meeting, and then the defense as a whole, his meetings would be interactive.

Enter players getting called upon before the group to confirm they know their assignments, quiz-style, and questions regularly welcome. The more mistakes and misinterpretations that can be corrected in meetings and practice, the better. The more communication, Parker and his staff figure, the fewer miscommunications.

So during training camp practices, it was not uncommon for seven or eight safeties (including some on the sideline at the time) to yell out a receiver formation at the same time nor was it uncommon for four to five linebackers to simultaneously yell "area, area, area," defensive backs coach and passing game coordinator Derrick Ansley said.

"Communication is a fundamental," Ansley told Yahoo Sports during training camp. "If you don't work at it, you're going to suck at it."

One game into the regular season, the Cowboys know they need work.

In the box score and on their Week 1 film, warts popped up to create, in Parker's estimation, "one poor performance."

Situational football concerns, like allowing the Giants to convert on 9-of-11 third downs, proved most glaring.

Dallas wasn't just allowing conversions on third-and-short.

Three times, the Giants faced third-and-9. All three times, quarterback Jaxson Dart found an outlet to convert.

"The one that really stands out to me [as] a big one, was we had a penalty, we got kicked back to third-and-9, and they ran a little bit of a non-traditional Tampa 2 defense," Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said of a play 40 seconds before halftime. "And they had a drop end and Jaxson threw the out route to [receiver] Malik [Nabers]. I think that's not an everyday coverage. And Jaxson saw that. He remained composed.

"And that was just one of those nine makes that we had."

In the fourth quarter, Dart would find running back Devin Singletary and tight end Isaiah Likely each to move the chains on a third-and-9.

Singletary's series drew plenty of attention as the Cowboys ceded three plays to Singletary in the left flat on the same drive.

Just before those three strikes, rookie linebacker Jaishan Barham had snuffed Singletary out in the backfield for a loss of 7 yards.Then Dart hit Singletary with a checkdown in the left flat and Singletary ran through safety Jalen Thompson and into first-down territory.

Singletary ran what looked, to viewers' untrained eye, via the same outlet for the touchdown that soon extended the Giants' lead to two scores.

The Giants' play calls differed each of the three times, Dart said. The Cowboys also said afterward that their assignments weren't identical even as their error echoed, perhaps not unrelated to Overshown's injury and a green dot transfer earlier that very drive.

"I felt like we had times we outleveraged them, whether it was just in the flats or just checkdowns," Dart said. "And our backs did an awesome job of being able to scan their protection responsibilities and to get out fast in the flats. And that makes it hard for the defense at times.

"[Singletary] did an unbelievable job of being able to kind of just hide, get out fast, and then just kind of felt space and the ball."

Parker didn't mince words on his unit's inability to get off the field, Dallas' defense dragged across 25 plays and 13:33 of the 15-minute fourth quarter.

"It's certainly unacceptable," he said, "what happened in the fourth quarter."

Facing Commanders, Cowboys won't worry about what's 'not our business'

On Wednesday night and into Thursday, a phenomenon that often greets the Cowboys greeted Parker, Barham and Dallas' defense.

The entertainment machine Jerry Jones built enjoys a bright spotlight. It also attracts loud noise and attention across social media and beyond that is prone to overreaction.

The latest example: a clip from NBC's broadcast of the Cowboys' game in which Parker appears to talk sternly to Barham.

A visibly emotional Barham, at one point, stands up from the bench, shaking off Parker who appears to be trying to continue the conversation.

The video had surpassed 3 million views in roughly 24 hours, even as some commented how frequently similar exchanges occur on the sideline. So Parker fielded a question about it during his news conference Thursday.

"I think he was frustrated," Parker said. "It's his first NFL game and things aren't going to be perfect. This isn't a fairy tale at all. And I think that Jaishawn cares as much as anybody in that locker room about us winning, No. 1, but, No. 2, our defensive performance.

"So he was a little frustrated with himself and frustrated with our side of the ball as we played. But I don't think anybody in our building has any doubt of what he's going to do coming real soon. So we don't have any reservations about his mentality. We welcome that passion. Have to channel it better. And that's something that young players have to go through. It's a natural progression.

"We have a lot of confidence in Jaishawn."

The answer spoke to the personality and coaching style the Cowboys expected to find when they hired Parker knowing that an overhaul in personnel and defensive structure would require some adjustments.

Parker did not act as if a disappointment did not occur, his realism that the NFL "isn't a fairy tale" blunt and direct. But he also didn't throw his players under the bus following a rough outing nor did he panic.

He took accountability and stood up for his players, his tone similarly level to his news conferences before his first game as play-caller faced struggles.

"One of the things I look for when I see good play-callers is Christian's very calm," Stephen Jones said in August. "He's steady in the boat and he's not over the top. And I think that's where you've got to be in a game to call the plays."

In meetings this week, too, Parker was "even-keeled," edge rusher Rashan Gary said. Gary's assessment: Parker was the "same."

Will the same approach fuel a different outcome in the Cowboys' second straight division game?

Parker has adjusted some of his weekly schedule based off the opener, retooling elements of the Cowboys' walkthrough format and shifting how they rep formation adjustments as well as verbal and nonverbal communication. He placed extra emphasis on signals and eye contact in anticipation of a loud home crowd against the Washington Commanders.

Linebackers and defensive backs will need to step up with Overshown and Hooker each out this week. Dart is the first in a string of mobile quarterbacks that threaten, the Commanders' Jayden Daniels next followed by the Baltimore Ravens ' Lamar Jackson .

Daniels accounted for 195 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday in a 24-22 loss to Parker's last employer, the Philadelphia Eagles . The Commanders also arrive with a receiver room they believe is their deepest unit on the team, from longtime WR1 Terry McLaurin to third-round rookie Antonio Williams to training camp pickup Stefon Diggs .

On the offensive line after left tackle Laremy Tunsil 's season-ending triceps tear, Washington could be vulnerable. If the Cowboys' rush can capitalize, their coverage won't need to carry as heavy a load.

And Parker reminds Dallas players that they, too, don't need to carry the exact load the outside voices are asking them, too. Last year's unraveling is "really not our business."

"We weren't here," Parker said of his staff. "This is the 2026 defense and it's our responsibility to fix our performance on Sunday. Not performances from 2024 or 2025 — just for us to fix our performances on Sunday.

"And I think everyone's been accountable and responsible for that."

Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams , whom the Cowboys extended during training camp, echoed that.

Parker copped to his growth areas with the team. Players followed suit.

"The guys we got in our locker room, man, [they're] unbelievable when it comes down to taking constructive criticism, it comes down to taking accountability," Williams told reporters after the game. "We had a lot of mental errors, a lot of busts today, and just really being critical with that going into this week and focus on getting better.

"We already said to each other: 'Bro, we hold each other accountable to get better.'"

articles.title: NFL: Josh Allen leads Buffalo Bills to victory in first game at Highmark Stadium
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills open their new stadium in style with a 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions, as Josh Allen again impresses.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills opened their new stadium in style with a 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.

After winning 36-31 at the Houston Texans in their first game of the season on Sunday, the Bills produced another impressive performance in their home opener.

They scored six touchdowns at Highmark Stadium, built next to their old home at a cost of $2.2bn (£1.6bn), with quarterback Josh Allen throwing for three and rushing for two more.

The Bills are among the favourites to represent the AFC Conference in the Super Bowl and raced into a 21-0 lead.

Allen barged into the endzone and found Joshua Palmer for a 43-yard touchdown, before Dawson Knox scored early in the second quarter.

The Lions replied with Jared Goff finding Jahmyr Gibbs, who became the NFL's highest-paid running back in the off-season, for an 11-yard touchdown catch.

But Dalton Kincaid stretched Buffalo's lead and the Bills remained comfortable throughout the second half.

Detroit, who beat the New Orleans Saints in overtime last week, cut the deficit with two touchdowns by Amon-Ra St Brown and another from Sam LaPorta.

But Allen, the NFL's Most Valuable Player for the 2024 season, and James Cook scored for the Bills to ensure the Lions only got within 10 points.

Before the game in Buffalo, which is on the US border with Canada, both the American and Canadian national anthems were played.

The latter was sung by Canadian band Barenaked Ladies as the Bills chose to honour their Canadian fans amid rising tensions between the two countries.

articles.title: ‘Specializes in Being Hurt’ — Former NFL LB Gets Brutally Honest About Joe Burrow’s Concerning Injury Status
articles.summary: Joe Burrow helped the Cincinnati Bengals open the 2026 season with a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but his latest injury update has already raised...
articles.body:
Joe Burrow helped the Cincinnati Bengals open the 2026 season with a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , but his latest injury update has already raised concerns. Back tightness limited Burrow's participation in practice on Wednesday and Thursday.

However, the Bengals quarterback has made it clear he plans to play Sunday against the Houston Texans . He even called the idea of sitting out "ridiculous." Still, former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho wasn't surprised to see Burrow dealing with another injury so early in the season.

Emmanuel Acho Questions Joe Burrow's Durability After Week 1

Speaking on "Speakeasy", Emmanuel Acho pointed to Joe Burrow's long injury history and questioned why the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback keeps dealing with physical issues.

"Of all the things I've never been surprised by in my life, I've never been surprised by this one first. Of course he's hurt. That's what Joe Burrow does. Specializes in being hurt. He's a killer on the field. One of the most talented quarterbacks in all of football… But of course, he's hurt," Acho said.

Burrow has already dealt with several major injuries during his NFL career. He tore the ACL, MCL, PCL, and meniscus in his left knee during his rookie season in 2020.

He later suffered a torn ligament in his throwing wrist in 2023 before dealing with a Grade 3 turf toe injury in 2025. Acho's biggest concern is that Burrow is already dealing with back tightness after just one game of the new season.

"Wildly disappointing. We're already dealing with back tightness. Bro, it's not like you balled out that crazy Week 1. Let the defense's back be tight. If anybody's back should be tight, let it be them, not you," Acho said.

Burrow did throw for 254 yards and a touchdown in the win over Tampa Bay , but he also threw a pick-six. Tampa Bay held Ja'Marr Chase to just two catches, leaving Cincinnati's passing game with plenty of room to improve.

Burrow has said the back tightness will not keep him from playing against Houston, but the matchup could test him physically.

The Texans have a strong defensive front, meaning Burrow will need to move comfortably in the pocket and avoid taking unnecessary hits. Cincinnati's offensive line will also have an important role in keeping pressure off its quarterback.

For now, Burrow says he will play. But after another early injury concern, his health remains one of the biggest storylines surrounding the Bengals.
